To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we developed an ontology based approach for the design and development of mediation information systems, (2) we defined a Collaboration Ontology and Collaboration Process Ontology that represent the knowledge of business partners and generic business processes respectively, (3) we defined a set of transformation rules in order to extract information to build the Collaborative Business Process (CBP) model, and (4) we defined a KBS to support the design and development process of mediation information systems.
we have developed a knowledge-based system for the design of collaborative business processes, and that we have defined an ontology for the collaborative business process modeling.

the use of ontologies in business process models allows the definition of the knowledge that is necessary to build collaborative business process models, and that the use of a KBS is necessary to support the knowledge-based reasoning in order to build the CBPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a knowledge-based system for the collaborative design of business processes.
a knowledge-based system that is able to capture and reuse knowledge from business partners and from generic existing knowledge in order to build an initial CBP model.
the development of an ontology-based approach to the design of a CBP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach is based on the use of ontologies to provide a formal representation for the knowledge gathered from the business partners.
the approach described in this paper is a good starting point for the design of mediation information system, which is the main purpose of this research.
the proposed ontology-based approach provides the necessary structure to build CBP model from knowledge captured from the business partners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed KBS is able to capture the knowledge from business partners in the CO, and to extract the knowledge to build the CPO, and finally, to use this knowledge to build a CBP model.
the proposed KBS is a first step towards a model driven engineering for the design of CBPs.
the CBP model is built from a high level abstraction of the business knowledge captured from the business partners, and from a generic business process knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ontologies in the design of a CBP model is an efficient way to represent and reason about knowledge from business partners.
the proposed KBS approach allows us to extract knowledge from business partners in a collaborative way in order to generate a business process model that is compliant to the business partners' needs.

it provides a way to extract the knowledge from business partners in order to build a collaborative business process model, and it also provides the knowledge to build the mediation system that is required in order to exchange data between business partners in the collaborative process.
